title: It Started With a Go-Kart for Sale
author: Nic Bailey
summary: Long before there was a team, there was a dream of getting behind the wheel. A Facebook ad helped turn that dream into the beginning of 313 Motorsports.
imageAlt: Original red number 313 kart at the track
body:
BEHIND THE CURTAIN · OUR JOURNEY

IT STARTED WITH A GO-KART FOR SALE.

By Nic Bailey · Founder, 313 Motorsports

Racing has always been a part of my life. Looking back, I guess it was only a matter of time before I found my own way into it.

My mom and grandfather were involved in drag racing, and my grandfather worked at Indianapolis Raceway Park. My dad worked for an IndyCar team, helping with data, wind tunnel operations, and IT services.

When I was 13, I moved to Speedway, Indiana. Growing up there, racing was everywhere. I spent a lot of time going to different racetracks, watching races, and taking in everything that came with being around motorsports.

I loved the sounds, the atmosphere, and the people. But more than anything, I always wanted to be the one behind the wheel.

The problem was, wanting to race and actually figuring out how to get started were two completely different things.

SOMETIMES ALL IT TAKES IS ONE OPPORTUNITY.

Fast-forward a few years, and I’m scrolling through Facebook when I come across an ad for a go-kart for sale.

Nothing fancy. Just a go-kart.

But something about it caught my attention. That dream of racing, the one I’d carried around since I was a kid, suddenly felt like something I could actually do.

I didn’t have some big plan to start a racing team. I didn’t know much about karting, and I definitely didn’t know what I was getting myself into.

I just knew I wanted to race.

That decision became the beginning of 313 Motorsports in 2023.

Even the name has a story behind it. For years, 313 had been part of family jokes and conversations about different business ideas. We always had something we were going to do someday.

313 Motorsports became the first one we actually turned into something real.

TWO LAPS DOWN AND A REALITY CHECK.

I remember going into my first race feeling a little bit of everything.

I was nervous. I was excited. And if I’m being completely honest, I was probably a whole lot more confident in my driving abilities than I had any business being.

I’d spent years watching racing, and somewhere in my head, I think I convinced myself that I had a pretty good idea of what I was doing.

Turns out, watching racing and actually racing are two very different things.

I finished my first race two laps down.

Two. Entire. Laps.

Needless to say, that wasn’t exactly the debut I’d pictured in my head.

I showed up thinking I knew a little something about racing. I left realizing just how much I didn’t know.

And somehow, I walked away with even more questions than I had when I arrived.

But here’s the funny thing.

Even after getting that reality check, I still wanted to come back.

Maybe more than ever.

LEARNING EVERYTHING THE HARD WAY.

That first race was just the beginning of a pretty steep learning curve.

The hardest part wasn’t necessarily finishing two laps down. It was leaving the track knowing I had a lot to learn, but not knowing who to talk to or where to start.

I didn’t really have anyone pointing me in the right direction. Most of what I learned in the beginning came through trial and error.

And trust me, there was plenty of error.

I’d try something, hope it worked, and sometimes end up with more questions than I started with. There were frustrating weekends, mistakes that probably could’ve been avoided, and moments when I wondered if I was ever going to figure this whole karting thing out.

But I kept showing up.

Race after race, I kept coming back because, no matter how frustrating things got, I still loved being at the track.

And eventually, something started to change.

After a few races, people in the karting community started reaching out, offering advice, answering questions, and helping me find my way.

I went from feeling like I was trying to figure everything out on my own to realizing there were people around me who genuinely wanted to see me improve.

That support meant more than I think those people realized.

It didn’t suddenly make me a better driver overnight, and I still had plenty to learn. But it made the challenges a little less overwhelming and reminded me why I loved being part of racing in the first place.

Looking back, I learned two things from those early experiences.

First, getting started in racing can be incredibly intimidating when you don’t know anyone or even know what questions to ask.

And second, sometimes all it takes is someone willing to share a little knowledge or encouragement to make a difference.

I’ve been on both sides of that experience. I’ve been the new guy who didn’t know where to turn, and I’ve experienced what it feels like when a racing community welcomes you in.

That’s the feeling I want people to have when they become part of 313 Motorsports.

BUILDING SOMETHING BIGGER THAN MYSELF.

When I first started 313 Motorsports, my goal was pretty simple. I wanted to race.

But somewhere along the way, that goal started to grow.

I began thinking about other people who might be standing where I once stood. People who have always wanted to race but don’t know where to begin. Parents whose kids dream of becoming drivers but have no idea how to get started.

I know what it’s like to have the passion without having the answers.

And I also know how much it means when someone takes the time to help.

That’s why I want 313 Motorsports to be more than a team that shows up on race weekends.

I want to build a racing family where people feel welcome, questions are encouraged, and drivers help each other grow.

I’m not going to pretend I have all the answers. I’m still learning myself.

But I’ve learned that racing is about more than what happens on the track. It’s about the people you meet, the relationships you build, and the opportunities you create for others.

If I can take what the karting community has given me and pass even a little of that along to the next person chasing their dream, then we’re building something worth being proud of.

Because at the end of the day, I don’t just want to build better drivers. I want to help give people the opportunity to chase something they’ve always wanted to do.

IF IT’S YOUR CALLING, IT WILL KEEP CALLING.

For years, I kept finding reasons to put racing off. There was always something else going on, something more important to take care of, or a reason why it wasn’t the right time.

But no matter how much time passed, that desire to race never went away.

Eventually, I realized I could keep waiting for the perfect opportunity, or I could take a chance and see where it led.

For me, that chance started with a Facebook ad for a go-kart.

And looking back, I’m glad I answered that call.

If it’s your calling, it will keep calling.

This is just the beginning of our story.
